title: Worksheet — Chemical Reactions and Equations (Class 10 CBSE Science)
instructions: Attempt all 10 questions. Show all balancing work and reasoning for the subjective questions. Total time: 50 minutes.

questions.question: The Law of Conservation of Mass requires:
options: mass of products = mass of reactants
questions.answer: mass of products = mass of reactants

questions.question: In a redox reaction, oxidation and reduction always happen together.
AB + CD → AD + CB is a ____ reaction.
The slow eating-away of metals by air and moisture is called:
Balance: Fe + H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + H₂. Show atom counts on each side.
questions.answer: 3 Fe + 4 H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + 4 H₂. Atoms — Fe: 3=3; H: 8=8; O: 4=4 ✓.

questions.question: Define and give one example each of: combination, decomposition, double displacement.
questions.answer: Combination: A + B → AB. Example: 2 Mg + O₂ → 2 MgO. Decomposition: AB → A + B. Example: 2 H₂O₂ → 2 H₂O + O₂. Double displacement: AB + CD → AD + CB. Example: AgNO₃ + NaCl → AgCl↓ + NaNO₃.

questions.question: In CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O, identify which substance is OXIDISED, which is REDUCED, and name the oxidising and reducing agents.
questions.answer: H₂ is OXIDISED (gains oxygen → becomes H₂O). CuO is REDUCED (loses oxygen → becomes Cu). The oxidising agent is CuO (provides oxygen). The reducing agent is H₂ (takes oxygen).

questions.question: Why does food packaging often contain antioxidants? Give one example of an antioxidant and explain its role.
questions.answer: Antioxidants prevent the oxidation of fats and oils in food, which would otherwise cause RANCIDITY (bad smell and taste). Example: BHA (butylated hydroxyanisole) or BHT. Role: they react with oxygen / free radicals before the fats do, so the food stays fresh longer.

questions.question: Balance the following four equations and classify each by reaction type. (a) Na + H₂O → NaOH + H₂. (b) ZnCO₃ → ZnO + CO₂. (c) AgNO₃ + KCl → AgCl + KNO₃. (d) C + O₂ → CO₂.
questions.answer: (a) 2 Na + 2 H₂O → 2 NaOH + H₂. Type: DISPLACEMENT (Na displaces H from water). (b) ZnCO₃ → ZnO + CO₂. Type: DECOMPOSITION (already balanced). (c) AgNO₃ + KCl → AgCl + KNO₃. Type: DOUBLE DISPLACEMENT (already balanced). (d) C + O₂ → CO₂. Type: COMBINATION (already balanced).

questions.question: An iron gate left outside develops rust. (i) Why does this happen — chemically? (ii) Why is rusting more rapid in coastal areas than in the desert? (iii) Suggest THREE ways to slow or prevent rusting and explain WHY each works.
questions.answer: (i) Iron reacts slowly with oxygen and moisture from the air to form HYDRATED IRON(III) OXIDE (Fe₂O₃·xH₂O), commonly called rust. (ii) Coastal areas have HIGH humidity AND salt particles in the air, which act as electrolytes that accelerate the rusting reaction. Deserts are dry, so rusting is slow. (iii) Three prevention methods: (1) PAINTING — physical barrier between iron and air. (2) GALVANISING (zinc coating) — zinc oxidises preferentially (sacrificial protection). (3) ALLOYING with chromium / nickel to make stainless steel — Cr forms a passive oxide layer that prevents further corrosion.
